The test image shows a soybean stem with a distinct pinkish/white cottony growth covering the stem. This looks like fungal mycelium on a stem. Key features:
- Stem covered in white/pink fluffy cottony fungal growth
- Some reddish/dark lesions visible on the stem
- Leaves appear mostly green (healthy-looking leaves surrounding)
- Affected part: stem

This strongly suggests White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot) - known for white cottony mycelium on stems. Let me check reference images for White Mold and a few other candidates.
White Mold reference shows white cottony mycelium with dark sclerotia on stem. The test image has similar white/pink cottony growth. Let me check more references.
Good - this White Mold reference shows white fluffy mycelium at a stem node, closer to the test image. Now let me check other stem-disease candidates to compare.

Phytophthora shows brown stem rot with wilting, Rhizoctonia shows purplish stem canker - neither matches the cottony white/pink growth in the test image. Let me check more classes to fulfill the 16-view requirement.
14 classes viewed so far. Need 2 more.

I've now viewed 16+ reference images across 16+ different classes. Here's my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean stem covered with prominent white/pink fluffy cottony fungal growth
- Some reddish/dark lesions visible along the stem
- Surrounding leaves appear green and healthy
- Classic stem-focused disease presentation

**Comparison with references:**
- **White_Mold**: Reference `Soybean_Dise_415.jpg` shows white fluffy mycelium at a stem node — this closely matches the cottony growth pattern in the test image. `Soybean_Dise_133.jpg` shows more advanced stage with sclerotia.
- **Phytophthora**: Shows brown water-soaked stem rot with wilting — no cottony growth.
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows purplish-brown stem canker near soil line — not matching.
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows internal brown pith discoloration — different symptom type.
- **All leaf-based diseases** (Cercospora, Septoria, Bacterial_Blight, Frogeye, etc.): Clearly leaf lesion patterns — not matching.

The white/pink fluffy cottony mycelium on the stem is the hallmark of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). No other class in the reference set shows this type of growth.
